close_reason: Bead's recommendation ratified: for 0.1.x keep the current Vec<String> / &[&str] surface; revisit as a 0.2.0 or 1.0-prep design pass. Follow-up design epic filed at bd:JMAP-tjvm.40 (P4, deferred) tracking the typed-property-selector design questions: const-tuple-struct pattern, header:* selector constructor, vendor-extensions vs workspace property-enum policy, sweep scope across 7 sibling crates, migration story. No 0.1.x code action; the current API surface works and typo bugs surface at runtime via spec-mandated server-side invalidArguments errors.
description:
mod.rs:45     EmailGetParams.body_properties: Option<Vec<String>>
mod.rs:260    EmailParseParams.properties: Option<Vec<String>>
mod.rs:263    EmailParseParams.body_properties: Option<Vec<String>>

Plus the per-method `properties: Option<&[&str]>` arguments on email_get, mailbox_get, thread_get, identity_get, email_submission_get, etc.

RFC 8621 enumerates the property names for each object type:

  Email properties (§4.1): id, blobId, threadId, mailboxIds, keywords, size,
    receivedAt, messageId, inReplyTo, references, sender, from, to, cc, bcc,
    replyTo, subject, sentAt, hasAttachment, preview, bodyValues, textBody,
    htmlBody, attachments, bodyStructure
  
  EmailBodyPart properties (§4.1.4): partId, blobId, size, name, type, charset,
    disposition, cid, language, location, subParts, headers, header:*,
    bodyStructure
  
  Mailbox properties (§2.1): id, name, parentId, role, sortOrder, totalEmails,
    unreadEmails, totalThreads, unreadThreads, myRights, isSubscribed
  
  Thread properties (§3.1): id, emailIds

Etc.

Defensive-code-forcing today: a caller writing `email_get(Some(&ids), Some(&["receivedAt", "from", "to"]), None)` and accidentally typing "receivedat" gets no compile-time signal. Behaviour depends on the server: spec-conformant servers SHOULD reject with invalidArguments, but lenient servers may silently return the default property set or ignore the unknown name.

Three design options:

  (a) Keep Vec<String> / &[&str]. Accept the trade-off.

  (b) Define a typed enum per object type with one variant per spec property name:

      #[non_exhaustive]
      #[derive(...)]
      pub enum EmailProperty {
          Id,
          BlobId,
          ThreadId,
          MailboxIds,
          // ...
          // Header(String) — RFC 8621 §4.1.2 allows header:Name selectors
      }

      Then properties: Option<&[EmailProperty]> on email_get.

  (c) Define typed PROPERTY-NAME constants on a struct (similar to the
     workspace's State / Id typed wrappers):

      pub struct EmailProperty(pub Cow<'static, str>);
      impl EmailProperty {
          pub const ID: Self = Self(Cow::Borrowed("id"));
          pub const BLOB_ID: Self = Self(Cow::Borrowed("blobId"));
          // ...
      }

Trade-offs:

  - Option (a) is what every callsite has today. Easiest to ship, hardest for callers.
  - Option (b) gives full typing but rules out vendor-extension property names unless the enum carries an Other(String) variant. Per workspace policy, property-selector enums are NOT in scope for the Unknown(String) pattern (workspace AGENTS.md), so a strict enum may be too rigid.
  - Option (c) gives ergonomic typed constants AND allows vendor extensions via the public tuple constructor. This matches the workspace's State / Id pattern.

Recommendation: (c), implemented in a follow-up bead. Defer because:

  1. The header:* selector pattern (RFC 8621 §4.1.2) needs a dedicated constructor on EmailProperty for the dynamic header name case, raising the design complexity.
  
  2. RFC 8621 has many object types; the typed-properties sweep is a 7-extension propagation per workspace canonical-template rule.

Priority P3 — meaningful API improvement but not a correctness bug. The current API works; typo bugs surface at runtime via server-side invalidArguments. Worth tracking as a 0.x → 1.0 follow-up.

Mark says NO HUMAN — Recommendation: option (c) as a 0.2.0 or 1.0-prep design epic. For 0.1.x, the current Vec<String> / &[&str] surface is acceptable.
